intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day longtail boat tour around the stunning Phi Phi archipelago, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Viking Cave, and swimming at Monkey Beach. One of Thailand's most iconic island-hopping experiences with breathtaking limestone karst scenery.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Crawl
experiences.description: Dive into Bangkok's legendary street food scene with a self-guided or guided evening crawl through Yaowarat (Chinatown) and nearby stalls. Sample pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh seafood. Yaowarat Road comes alive after dark with sizzling woks and vibrant energy.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta & Koh Rok Snorkeling Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a speedboat from Koh Lanta to the remote and pristine Koh Rok islands, known for their untouched coral reefs, turquoise lagoons, and abundant marine life including sea turtles and reef sharks. Far less crowded than Phi Phi, this is a hidden gem for beach and snorkeling lovers.
experiences.location: Koh Rok, Koh Lanta District, Krabi

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Sunday Walking Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through Chiang Mai's famous Sunday Night Market along Wualai Road, sampling northern Thai specialties like khao soi (coconut curry noodles), sai oua (herbed sausage), mango sticky rice, and crispy pork rinds. Combine food tasting with local handicraft shopping and cultural street performances.
experiences.location: Wualai Road, Old City, Chiang Mai

experiences.name: Similan Islands Full-Day Snorkeling Expedition
experiences.description: Join a guided boat tour to the world-renowned Similan Islands National Park, consistently ranked among the top dive and snorkel destinations globally. Explore vibrant coral gardens, swim alongside whale sharks (seasonal), and relax on powdery white sand beaches with impossibly clear Andaman Sea waters.
experiences.location: Similan Islands National Park, Phang Nga Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take a budget shuttle or minivan to the pier (Rassada Pier in Phuket or Ao Nang Pier in Krabi depending on routing). Purchase a ferry ticket to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 150–250 THB). Board the afternoon ferry and enjoy scenic views of the Andaman Sea on the way to Ko Phi Phi Don.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phi Phi Don, check into your Boutique Stay accommodation. Drop off bags and freshen up. Take a short walk along the main village strip (Tonsai Village) to get oriented. Explore the lively beachfront night scene.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip — arrival day
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport food court or 7-Eleven convenience store (pad kra pao rice box ~60 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village street food stalls — try pad thai or grilled satay skewers (80–120 THB per dish)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance if possible during peak season. October can bring occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket. Exchange some cash at the airport for better rates before heading to the islands.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (Pha Chee Viewpoint) for a stunning panoramic view of the twin bays of Ko Phi Phi Don. The hike takes about 20–30 minutes and costs around 30 THB entry. Best visited before 9:00 AM to avoid crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Long Beach (Hat Yao) on the southeastern side of the island — reachable by a short longtail boat ride (~50 THB) or 20-minute walk. Swim in calm, clear turquoise water and relax on the less-crowded beach. Snorkel around the coral reefs near the shore (bring your own snorkel gear or rent for ~100 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and stroll the main walking street. Watch the sunset from Tonsai Bay beachfront. Join a free fire show on the beach (common at local bars in the evening). Enjoy a cold Chang beer from a beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or guesthouse breakfast near Tonsai — toast with eggs and coffee (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Beach shack at Long Beach — coconut rice with grilled fish (~100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant or local Thai eatery in Tonsai Village — green curry with rice (~120 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy sandals or sneakers for the viewpoint hike. Bring sunscreen and water. The viewpoint is free to walk up but some paths charge a small fee — 30 THB is typical.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling tour departing from Tonsai Pier (approx. 500–700 THB for a half-day tour). Visit iconic spots including Maya Bay (of 'The Beach' fame), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave. Tours typically depart at 8:00–9:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snorkeling tour — swim with tropical fish and explore the dramatic limestone cliffs of Phi Phi Leh. Return to Tonsai by early afternoon. Relax on Tonsai Beach or Loh Dalum Bay and dry off in the sun.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tonsai Village night market for cheap eats and souvenirs. Try mango sticky rice from a street vendor. Watch the nightly fire dancers perform on Loh Dalum Bay beach.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and banana pancake from a street stall near the pier (~60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in some group tours OR pack snacks — instant noodles, fruit, crackers from 7-Eleven
meals.dinner: Night market in Tonsai — pad see ew noodles and fresh pineapple (~100 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has regulated visitor numbers and timed entry — your group tour operator should handle this. October weather may affect sea conditions; check with operators the morning of the tour. Book group tours (not private) to keep costs low.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak from Tonsai Beach (approx. 150–200 THB per hour) and paddle around the coastline toward Monkey Beach. Watch the resident macaque monkeys from a safe distance — do not feed them. Explore sea caves and hidden coves accessible only by water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return kayak and head to the quieter Loh Moo Dee Bay on the eastern side of the island for a peaceful afternoon swim. Read, nap in a hammock, or simply enjoy the solitude away from the main tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Cook your own dinner challenge — visit the small local market near the back of Tonsai Village and pick up fresh ingredients. Alternatively, find a local Thai restaurant away from the beachfront (prices are significantly lower, ~80–100 THB per dish). Try tom kha soup.

meals.breakfast: Coconut pancakes and fresh fruit from a beachside stall (~70 THB)
meals.lunch: Simple fried rice with egg from a local shop (~60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Off-the-beaten-path Thai restaurant in the village interior — tom yum soup and jasmine rice (~100–120 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking is best done in the morning before winds pick up. Monkey Beach monkeys can be aggressive — keep bags closed and avoid direct eye contact. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approx. 250–300 THB, journey ~1.5–2 hours). Arrive in Krabi Town mid-morning. Drop bags at a budget guesthouse or left-luggage service at the pier. Explore Krabi Town's charming riverside walking street and the famous Krabi Town Walking Street market area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram — a stunning white Buddhist temple perched on a hill above Krabi Town with golden Buddha statues and panoramic views (free entry). Walk through the local fresh market near Maharaj Road to see exotic fruits, spices, and street food.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Krabi Town Night Market (open from 5:00 PM) along the riverside promenade. Sample an enormous variety of street food — grilled seafood, rotis, som tam (papaya salad), and fresh coconut juice.

meals.breakfast: Early morning snack at Phi Phi pier before ferry — roti with condensed milk (~40 THB)
meals.lunch: Krabi Town local restaurant — khao man gai (chicken rice) (~60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Night Market — build your own meal from multiple stalls (budget 150–200 THB for a full spread)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance — morning ferries from Phi Phi to Krabi typically depart at 9:00 AM. Krabi Town is a great base for exploring the surrounding region. Budget guesthouses in Krabi Town start from 300–500 THB per night.

day_by_day.morning: Take a songthaew (shared red truck taxi, ~50 THB) to Railay Beach — accessible only by longtail boat from Krabi Town pier (~100 THB per person). Arrive at Railay West Beach and walk the short path to Railay East. Begin the hike to Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of Thailand's most spectacular beaches, flanked by towering limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Phra Nang Cave (Princess Cave) — a sacred shrine filled with colorful offerings. Swim in the crystal-clear water of Phra Nang Beach. Attempt the short but steep hike to the lagoon viewpoint above Railay (free, but bring good shoes — ropes assist the climb).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by longtail and songthaew. Visit the riverside area for a relaxed evening. Try a cheap Thai massage on the walking street (200–250 THB per hour).

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local coffee shop near pier — toast, eggs, Nescafé (~70 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside vendor at Railay — fresh fruit platter and coconut water (~80 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town riverside restaurant — massaman curry with roti (~130 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is only accessible by boat — no roads connect it to the mainland. Longtail boats run frequently from Krabi Nopparat Thara pier. The lagoon hike involves ropes and muddy terrain — not suitable after heavy rain. October may bring rain; always check conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget 4-island tour departing from Krabi (approx. 500–650 THB including longtail boat, snorkel gear, and lunch). Visit Koh Mor, Koh Chuak, Koh Tub, and the famous Koh Poda — all featuring pristine white sand beaches and coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the 4-island tour — snorkel at Koh Poda and relax on its powdery white beach. Enjoy the included lunch on board or at a beach shack. Return to Krabi by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at guesthouse. Head out for a sunset walk along Ao Nang Beach (15-minute songthaew ride from Krabi Town, ~30 THB). Browse the Ao Nang walking street for cheap souvenirs and street food.

meals.breakfast: Local noodle soup (kuay teow) from a morning street stall (~50–60 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in 4-island tour OR fresh seafood at a beach shack (~150 THB)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang street food — grilled prawns on skewers and sticky rice (~120 THB)

day_by_day.notes: 4-island tours are widely available from Krabi piers — shop around for the best price. Group tours are much cheaper than private charters. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral ecosystems.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget minivan from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approx. 250–300 THB including ferry crossings, journey ~2 hours). Check into a budget bungalow on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — one of Koh Lanta's most beautiful and affordable beaches. Unpack and take a morning walk along the 4km stretch of beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter to explore Koh Lanta (approx. 200–250 THB per day — bring your license). Ride to Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) on the southeastern tip — a charming village of wooden stilted houses built over the sea, home to the island's original Sea Gypsy community. Explore the colorful shophouses and local craft stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the western beach (Long Beach or Klong Nin Beach). Find a beachfront bar with cheap happy hour drinks (beer from 60 THB). Enjoy the laid-back Lanta vibe.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure from Krabi — market breakfast (~60 THB)
meals.lunch: Old Town seafood restaurant — fresh fish with rice (~130–160 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront bungalow restaurant — red curry with coconut milk (~120 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less commercialized than Phi Phi — perfect for budget travelers. October is shoulder season so accommodation deals are plentiful. Scooter rental requires a valid motorcycle license; drive carefully on unpaved roads.

day_by_day.morning: Ride your scooter to Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island (entry fee: 200 THB for foreigners). Hike through jungle trails to a lighthouse with panoramic views of the Andaman Sea. Spot wildlife including monitor lizards, hornbills, and macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Klong Nin Beach on the way back — a quieter, more secluded beach popular with long-stay budget travelers. Swim and snorkel in the calm water. Alternatively, visit one of Koh Lanta's inland waterfalls (Khlong Chak or Than Mayom) accessible by scooter.
day_by_day.evening: Return scooter and relax on Long Beach for the sunset. Join a bonfire gathering at a beachside bar. Try a local cooking class if available (some budget options run for 500–700 THB including ingredients and a meal).

meals.breakfast: Bungalow breakfast — scrambled eggs, toast, fresh juice (~90 THB)
meals.lunch: National Park area — packed lunch from a 7-Eleven or simple roadside stall (~80 THB)
meals.dinner: Klong Dao Beach night market (if operating) or bungalow restaurant — pad thai with tofu (~100 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The national park lighthouse hike is moderate difficulty — wear closed-toe shoes. Bring plenty of water and insect repellent. October rain can make jungle trails slippery — proceed with caution.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry and minivan transfer from Koh Lanta back toward the Trang Province area or directly to Koh Mook (approx. 350–450 THB total). Koh Mook is a quieter, budget-friendly island with the famous Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot). Check into a simple beach bungalow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Emerald Cave — accessible only by swimming or kayaking through a 80-meter dark tunnel at low tide, which opens into a hidden inland beach surrounded by towering cliffs. Join a longtail boat trip from the pier (~200 THB) or swim independently at low tide. Absolutely unmissable.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on Sivalai Beach or Charlie Beach — two of the most beautiful beaches on Koh Mook. Watch the sunset from the beach with a cold drink. Enjoy the peaceful, unhurried island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab food at Koh Lanta pier or on the ferry
meals.lunch: Simple beachside restaurant on Koh Mook — fried rice with seafood (~100–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse restaurant — grilled barracuda with steamed rice and som tam (~150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The Emerald Cave can only be entered at low tide — check tide times before visiting. The swim through the dark cave is about 80 meters and requires basic swimming ability. Bring a waterproof phone case or dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak from your guesthouse (~150 THB per hour) and paddle around Koh Mook's coastline, exploring sea caves, mangroves, and secluded beaches. Alternatively, take a longtail boat to nearby Koh Kradan — rated one of Thailand's most beautiful islands with exceptional snorkeling directly off the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Koh Kradan's beach — snorkel over the coral reef that begins just meters from the shore. The water is exceptionally clear and marine life is abundant. Return to Koh Mook by late afternoon longtail.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner on Koh Mook — splurge slightly on a fresh seafood BBQ platter at a beachside restaurant (~250–300 THB). Watch the stars from the beach — minimal light pollution on this small island makes stargazing exceptional.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — fruit salad, yogurt, and coffee (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Koh Kradan beach shack — coconut curry soup and rice (~120 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachside seafood BBQ on Koh Mook — splurge meal for the trip (~250–300 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Kradan day trips can be arranged through your guesthouse or at the pier (~300–400 THB round trip by longtail). This area of Trang Province is significantly less touristy than Krabi or Phi Phi — enjoy the authenticity.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry back toward Trang or Krabi. If returning via Trang, visit Trang Town for a few hours — explore the vibrant Trang Morning Market, famous for its dim sum and Chinese-Thai breakfast culture (unique to this region). Try khanom jeen (fermented rice noodles with curry) for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel onward to Bangkok via overnight bus or budget flight (book in advance — AirAsia or Nok Air offer flights from Trang or Krabi for 500–1,500 THB if booked early). If taking the overnight bus, depart from Trang Bus Terminal in the evening. Arrive in Bangkok the following morning. Use the afternoon to rest at a budget guesthouse near Khao San Road or Silom.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Bangkok's Khao San Road area — the legendary backpacker hub. Browse the street market, try cheap cocktails from street vendors, and soak in the chaotic, vibrant energy. Visit Wat Chana Songkhram nearby (free entry, open until 9 PM).

meals.breakfast: Trang Morning Market — dim sum, coffee, and khanom jeen (~80–100 THB for a full spread)
meals.lunch: Airport or bus station food court (~80 THB)
meals.dinner: Khao San Road street food — pad thai, mango sticky rice, fresh spring rolls (~150 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Bangkok transport (flight or bus) well in advance to secure budget prices. Overnight buses from Trang to Bangkok take approximately 10–12 hours and cost around 500–700 THB. Budget flights can be cheaper if booked early. Khao San Road area has many guesthouses from 300–600 THB per night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bangkok — visit Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha) near the Grand Palace area (entry: 200 THB). Marvel at the 46-meter golden reclining Buddha and explore the beautiful temple complex. Afterward, take a quick boat ride along the Chao Phraya River on a public express boat (~15 THB) for scenic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Chatuchak Weekend Market (if visiting on a Saturday or Sunday) — the world's largest weekend market with thousands of stalls selling everything from street food to vintage clothing (free entry). Alternatively, explore the Silom area or do last-minute souvenir shopping at MBK Center. Make your way to the airport via the Airport Rail Link from Phaya Thai Station (~45 THB — fastest and cheapest airport transfer).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bangkok — farewell to Thailand! Reflect on 13 days of island hopping, street food feasting, and incredible Andaman Sea adventures.

meals.breakfast: Khao San Road area café — American breakfast or Thai-style congee (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Chatuchak Market food stalls — grilled pork skewers, papaya salad, fresh coconut (~120 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or pre-departure snack — 7-Eleven or airport food court (~100 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Suvarnabhumi Airport. The Airport Rail Link departs from Phaya Thai Station every 15 minutes and takes 30 minutes to the airport — far cheaper than a taxi. Declare any food items purchased at markets before boarding your international flight.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Phuket International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Rassada Pier. Board the ferry to Phi Phi Don Island (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Bay to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village walking streets. Browse local shops, watch the sunset from the beachfront, and soak in the island atmosphere after your journey.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during your layover
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Phuket airport food court or a café near Rassada Pier — try a Thai green curry rice box (฿80–120)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Papaya Restaurant in Tonsai Village — classic Thai dishes like pad kra pao and tom yum soup at mid-range prices (฿150–300 per dish)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry transfer in advance or purchase tickets at the pier. Arrive at Rassada Pier by 14:30 to catch an afternoon ferry. Keep your first evening relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk to Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–40 min hike). Enjoy panoramic views over both bays of Phi Phi Don — one of Thailand's most iconic vistas. Return for a leisurely breakfast near the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Leh. Visit Maya Bay (check current access rules), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave. Snorkel in the crystal-clear turquoise waters among colorful reef fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and enjoy the vibrant beachfront bar scene. Watch fire shows on the beach — a nightly Phi Phi tradition — and enjoy cocktails at a beachside bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or nearby café — fruit smoothie bowl and toast (฿120–180)
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch from a local bakery before the boat tour, or eat at a beachside shack on the tour stop
meals.dinner: Street food dinner along Tonsai walking street — grilled satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh spring rolls (฿200–350 total)

day_by_day.notes: Book the longtail boat tour through your hotel or a local operator the evening before. Maya Bay has restricted visiting hours and rules — confirm current regulations. Bring sunscreen, reef-safe if possible, a hat, and water.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at Long Beach (Haad Yao) on Phi Phi Don — a quieter, less crowded alternative to Tonsai Beach. Swim, snorkel off the shore, or simply relax on the sand with a good book.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat to Monkey Beach for a fun wildlife encounter (keep a safe distance from the monkeys). Continue to Bamboo Island for pristine white sand and shallow snorkeling waters. Spend 2–3 hours exploring before heading back.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a cooking class or food experience in Tonsai Village — learn to make pad thai and som tum from a local chef. Many operators offer 2-hour evening classes.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel — iced coffee and banana pancakes, a Thai-style street breakfast (฿100–150)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beach shack on Bamboo Island or pack snacks for the boat trip
meals.dinner: Eat the dishes you cooked in your cooking class, or dine at a mid-range restaurant in Tonsai — try massaman curry with roti (฿180–280)

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats to Long Beach, Monkey Beach, and Bamboo Island can be hired privately or shared. Negotiate prices at the pier or book through your hotel. October can bring occasional afternoon showers — carry a light rain poncho.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hours). Check into a guesthouse or leave luggage at a storage facility. Explore Krabi Town's charming riverside area and the famous Maharaj Street Night Market area by day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb the famous 1,237 steps to the summit for sweeping views over Krabi Province and the surrounding jungle. Allow 2–3 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's Chao Fa Night Market — one of the best street food markets in southern Thailand. Sample local specialties including grilled seafood, roti with condensed milk, and fresh fruit shakes.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Phi Phi hotel before the ferry departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Krabi Town at a local restaurant — khao man gai (Hainanese chicken rice) or boat noodles (฿60–120)
meals.dinner: Chao Fa Night Market street food feast — budget ฿200–400 for a full spread of snacks, mains, and desserts

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes, bring plenty of water, and avoid midday heat. The night market runs Thursday–Sunday evenings; confirm it is operating on this date. Store luggage at the ferry terminal or a nearby café if not staying in Krabi Town overnight.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Krabi Town to the Four Islands (Koh Mor, Koh Tub, Koh Chicken, and Koh Kwang). Depart early morning for the best light and fewer crowds. Snorkel at coral-rich spots and walk the famous sandbar connecting two islands at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour with a stop at Phra Nang Cave Beach — widely considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Thailand. Swim in the emerald waters and explore the cave shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang by longtail boat. Stroll along Ao Nang Beach promenade at sunset and browse the beachfront restaurants and shops.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a guesthouse or café in Krabi Town before departure — rice porridge (jok) with egg is a popular local option (฿60–90)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by most Four Islands tour operators, or eat at a beachside restaurant on Phra Nang Beach
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ao Nang at Last Fisherman Bar or a similar mid-range beachfront restaurant — fresh grilled fish with garlic and pepper (฿250–400)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Four Islands tour through a local operator in Krabi Town or Ao Nang. Tours typically run 9:00–16:00. The sandbar at Koh Tub is only accessible at low tide — check tide times in advance. Consider staying in Ao Nang tonight for easier access to tomorrow's activities.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day rock climbing lesson on the limestone karsts above Railay Beach — Krabi is world-famous for its climbing. Beginner-friendly routes are available with certified local instructors. Access Railay by longtail boat from Ao Nang (15 min).
day_by_day.afternoon: After climbing, relax on Railay West Beach — one of the most beautiful beaches in Krabi. Swim, kayak along the karst coastline, or simply lounge in the shade. Explore the short jungle trail to Railay East and the Lagoon viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the longtail back to Ao Nang before dark. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and an early night to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Ao Nang before heading to Railay — fruit smoothie and eggs at a beachfront café (฿120–180)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant on Railay Beach — fresh coconut, pad see ew noodles, or a seafood wrap (฿150–250)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ao Nang at a local Thai restaurant away from the main tourist strip for better value — green curry with jasmine rice (฿160–220)

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is only accessible by longtail boat — there is no road access. Longtails run frequently from Ao Nang pier (฿100–150 per person each way). Rock climbing tours can be booked through operators on Railay or in Ao Nang. Wear comfortable, flexible clothing for climbing.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: take a minivan or bus from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approx. 2–3 hours including ferry crossings). Check into your accommodation on Koh Lanta and take a brief orientation walk along Long Beach (Haad Yao).
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a charming historic fishing village with wooden stilt houses, Chinese-Thai shophouses, and a relaxed local atmosphere. Visit the local market and browse artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the west coast of Koh Lanta — the sunsets here are spectacular. Head to a beachfront bar for sundowners and enjoy the quieter, more laid-back island vibe.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Ao Nang before departure — roti with egg and tea, a classic Thai-Muslim breakfast (฿80–120)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Koh Lanta Old Town at a local seafood restaurant — grilled squid and steamed rice (฿150–200)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Long Beach — try the local specialty of massaman curry with fresh fish (฿200–320)

day_by_day.notes: Minivan transfers from Krabi to Koh Lanta can be booked through guesthouses or travel agencies. The journey includes two short ferry crossings. Scooter rental on Koh Lanta costs approximately ฿200–300/day — drive carefully on unpaved roads. Koh Lanta has a more relaxed pace than Phi Phi or Ao Nang.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koh Lanta Marine National Park — take a longtail boat to the park's islands including Koh Rok (if open in October) or Koh Ha for exceptional snorkeling and diving in protected waters with diverse coral and marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at a second island stop within the marine park. Look for sea turtles, reef sharks, and colorful tropical fish. Many tour operators include lunch on a secluded beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta and visit a local spa for a traditional Thai massage — a perfect way to unwind after a day in the water. Budget approximately ฿300–500 for a 1-hour massage.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a local café near Long Beach — fresh papaya, yogurt, and granola (฿100–150)
meals.lunch: Lunch included with most marine park tours — typically a simple Thai meal served on the beach
meals.dinner: Dinner at Drunken Sailors or a similar mid-range restaurant on Koh Lanta — wood-fired pizza or Thai-Western fusion (฿250–400)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is part of the marine national park and may have seasonal closures — confirm availability in October. Book the snorkeling tour the evening before. Koh Ha is generally accessible year-round and offers excellent snorkeling. Bring an underwater camera or waterproof phone case.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mu Ko Lanta National Park on the southern tip of Koh Lanta. Hike through mangrove forests, visit the park's lighthouse with panoramic views, and spot wildlife including monitor lizards and tropical birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Klong Nin Beach or Kantiang Bay — two of Koh Lanta's most beautiful and less-crowded beaches. Swim, relax, and enjoy the natural scenery of the west coast.
day_by_day.evening: Travel day preparation: pack bags for tomorrow's move. Enjoy a final dinner on Koh Lanta with a beachside barbecue experience — many restaurants offer fresh seafood grilled to order on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or a local bakery — fresh fruit shake and toast with local jam (฿80–130)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a small local restaurant near Kantiang Bay — tom kha gai soup and steamed jasmine rice (฿120–180)
meals.dinner: Beachside barbecue dinner — select fresh seafood (prawns, fish, squid) by weight and have it grilled — budget ฿400–600 for a full meal

day_by_day.notes: The national park entrance fee is approximately ฿200 for foreign visitors. The lighthouse hike is moderate — wear sturdy shoes. Klong Nin Beach is accessible by scooter (approx. 20 min from Long Beach). This is a great day to slow down and enjoy Koh Lanta's natural beauty before moving on.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry or speedboat from Koh Lanta to Koh Phi Phi Don (approx. 1.5 hours) or directly to Phuket (approx. 2 hours). Arrive in Phuket and check into a guesthouse in Patong or Kata Beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Kata Beach or Karon Beach — both are excellent mid-range alternatives to the busier Patong Beach. Swim, rent a surfboard (October can have good surf), or simply relax and enjoy the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Patong's Bangla Road in the evening for a taste of Phuket's famous nightlife — even if just for people-watching. Visit the night market stalls for street food and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast on Koh Lanta before the ferry — grab a takeaway roti and coffee from a beachside stall (฿60–100)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Phuket after arriving — try a local restaurant in Kata or Karon for khao pad (Thai fried rice) with seafood (฿120–180)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Patong Night Market or Malin Plaza — pad thai, grilled pork skewers, and mango sticky rice (฿200–350 total)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules between Koh Lanta and Phuket vary by season — book tickets the day before. In October, seas can be slightly rougher; speedboats may not operate on rough-weather days. Kata and Karon are more family-friendly and mid-range compared to Patong. Consider staying in Kata for a quieter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Phang Nga Bay — one of Thailand's most dramatic landscapes. Join a sea kayaking tour through limestone caves, hongs (enclosed lagoons), and mangrove tunnels. James Bond Island (Koh Tapu) is a highlight of this area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Phang Nga Bay tour with a visit to the floating Muslim fishing village of Koh Panyee — a fascinating community built entirely on stilts over the water. Have lunch here and explore the village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed evening at Kata or Karon Beach watching the sunset. Treat yourself to a seafood dinner at one of the beachfront restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a nearby café before the early tour departure (฿100–160)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Koh Panyee floating village — fresh seafood and local Thai dishes served at the village restaurants (฿150–250)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Kata or Karon — grilled whole snapper with lime and chili (฿300–450)

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay tours depart from Phuket Town or Ao Por Pier — book through your hotel or a reputable travel agency. Full-day tours typically cost ฿1,200–2,000 per person including transport, kayaking, and lunch. Bring a dry bag for your belongings during kayaking. October weather can be variable — tours may be adjusted based on conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-recognized area with beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture, colorful shophouses, and vibrant street art. Visit Thalang Road, Soi Rommanee, and the weekend market if timing aligns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Chalong — Phuket's largest and most revered Buddhist temple. Explore the ornate buildings, learn about the temple's history, and observe local worshippers. Afterward, visit the Big Buddha statue on Nakkerd Hill for panoramic views over the island.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Phuket — enjoy a traditional Thai dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant in Phuket Town such as Raya House or a similar heritage restaurant. Afterward, explore the Phuket Weekend Night Market (Naka Market) if it falls on a weekend.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Phuket Old Town at a Chinese-Thai café — dim sum, Chinese tea, and kaya toast (฿100–160)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Phuket Town — try Phuket's signature dishes: mee hokkien (Hokkien noodles) or o-tao (oyster omelette) (฿80–150)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Raya Restaurant or a similar mid-range heritage restaurant in Phuket Old Town — Phuket-style yellow curry and stir-fried local vegetables (฿250–400)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot — wear comfortable walking shoes. The Big Buddha is accessible by taxi or rented scooter (฿200–300 by taxi each way). Modest clothing (shoulders and knees covered) is required at Wat Chalong. Naka Market runs on weekends — confirm the schedule for this date.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last swim at your beach of choice. Do any remaining souvenir shopping at local markets or shops. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, spend remaining hours relaxing at the beach or pool, or visit a local spa for a final Thai massage. Transfer to Phuket International Airport (allow 1.5–2 hours before departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phuket International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of island hopping, street food adventures, and Thai culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — jok (rice porridge) with pork and ginger, or a classic American breakfast at a beach café (฿120–200)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near your hotel or at the airport — a final bowl of tom yum soup or pad thai to close out the culinary journey (฿150–250)
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Phuket International Airport if departing in the evening — or eat before heading to the airport

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and plan airport transfer accordingly. Phuket airport is approximately 30–45 minutes from Patong/Kata Beach depending on traffic. Allow extra time during peak hours. Purchase any last-minute Thai snacks (dried mango, coconut cookies, chili paste) as edible souvenirs at the airport duty-free or local convenience stores.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and collect luggage. Arrange a pre-booked private transfer to the pier, then board a luxury speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to the boutique stay, unwind on the private terrace, and take a refreshing dip in the pool overlooking the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Phi Phi Don waterfront at sunset. Explore the vibrant walking street for an introduction to local Thai street food — sample fresh grilled satay, mango sticky rice, and coconut ice cream from artisan vendors.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (travelling)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi Don — a beloved fine-casual spot known for fresh seafood, Thai curries, and wood-fired dishes with candlelit ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange speedboat transfer in advance to avoid delays at the pier. October sits at the tail end of the monsoon season — seas are generally calming but pack a light rain jacket. Check-in is typically 14:00–15:00; request early luggage drop if arriving ahead of schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided sunrise kayaking tour around the dramatic limestone karsts of Phi Phi Leh. Paddle through the iconic Viking Cave and glide into hidden lagoons with emerald-green water, accompanied by a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a premium half-day snorkelling excursion to Shark Point and Hin Bida Marine Park. Swim alongside leopard sharks, sea turtles, and vibrant reef fish. Return to the resort for a poolside lunch and a relaxing afternoon spa treatment — opt for a traditional Thai herbal compress massage.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking Tonsai Bay. Watch the sky turn gold and pink over the Andaman Sea before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platter, eggs Benedict, freshly pressed juices, and Thai-style rice congee at the boutique stay's open-air breakfast terrace
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled tiger prawns, papaya salad, and fresh coconut water at the resort's beach club
meals.dinner: Pee Pee Bakery & Restaurant — known for its fresh catch of the day, lobster thermidor, and authentic Thai massaman curry in a relaxed beachfront setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkelling excursion and spa treatment the evening before to secure preferred time slots. Marine park entry fees apply — typically included in premium tour packages.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a private full-day island-hopping speedboat charter. First stop: Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh — arrive early (before 10:00) to experience the iconic bay with fewer crowds. Swim in the crystal-clear shallows and explore the surrounding cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping journey to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) — a pristine sandbar island with powdery white sand and shallow turquoise waters perfect for swimming and sunbathing. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort and served on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Freshen up at the boutique stay, then explore the night market for authentic street food — look for pad thai cooked fresh to order, grilled seafood skewers, and mango salad.

meals.breakfast: Full Thai breakfast at the resort — jasmine rice soup, stir-fried vegetables, soft-boiled eggs, and tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Private gourmet beach picnic on Bamboo Island — prepared by the resort: fresh baguettes, cold cuts, local cheeses, tropical fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Local street food exploration at the Phi Phi night market — budget a tasting tour across multiple stalls for a premium authentic experience

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visiting hours and a daily visitor cap to protect the ecosystem — confirm access timings with your charter operator. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag, and extra water for the full day at sea.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private longtail boat to the quieter eastern side of Phi Phi Don. Hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint — a 20-minute moderate climb rewarded with one of Thailand's most breathtaking panoramic views over both bays. Bring a camera for golden-hour morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely afternoon. Arrange a private Thai cooking class at a local culinary studio — learn to prepare three signature dishes: tom kha gai (coconut galangal soup), green curry, and mango sticky rice using fresh market ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your culinary class for a private dinner experience, or dine at a waterfront restaurant with a tasting menu showcasing the best of southern Thai cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowls, avocado toast with chilli flakes, and freshly brewed Thai coffee at the resort
meals.lunch: Post-hike refreshment at a local café — iced Thai tea, fresh spring rolls, and a light noodle soup
meals.dinner: Mattaya Beach Restaurant — beachfront dining with a curated southern Thai tasting menu, fresh grilled barracuda, and house-made coconut desserts

day_by_day.notes: The viewpoint hike involves uneven stone steps — wear sturdy sandals or trainers. The cooking class typically lasts 3–4 hours and includes a market visit; book at least one day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands by private speedboat to Krabi Town (approximately 45 minutes). Check in to a luxury riverside boutique hotel in Krabi. After freshening up, visit the famous Krabi Town Weekend Market (Thanon Khong Kha Walking Street) for an immersive street food experience — sample roti with banana and condensed milk, fresh oysters, and local desserts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb the legendary 1,237 steps to the summit for sweeping views over Krabi's karst landscape and rice paddies. A physically rewarding cultural highlight.
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset longtail boat cruise along the Krabi River through mangrove forests, watching for kingfishers and monitor lizards as the sun dips below the limestone cliffs.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Phi Phi boutique stay — full tropical spread before departure
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at Krabi Town market — pad see ew, fresh fruit, and Thai iced coffee
meals.dinner: Krua Thara Restaurant, Krabi — a riverside institution known for its fresh seafood platters, steamed fish with lime and garlic, and authentic southern Thai dishes

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb takes approximately 45–60 minutes one way. Wear modest clothing (shoulders and knees covered) as it is an active Buddhist temple. Carry water — the climb can be strenuous in humidity.

day_by_day.morning: Join a premium full-day Four Islands tour by private speedboat from Krabi. First stop: Koh Poda — a stunning island with white sand beaches and excellent snorkelling around the surrounding reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Chicken Island (Koh Kai) for swimming and beach time, then Tup Island — a unique island connected by a sandbar that appears at low tide. Finish at Phra Nang Cave Beach, one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches, accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi by late afternoon. Visit the Chao Fah Pier area for a relaxed evening walk, then head to Viva Bar & Restaurant for cocktails with river views before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — American and Thai options, fresh juices, and local pastries
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on Koh Poda beach — provided by the private tour operator: fresh sandwiches, tropical fruit, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Ruen Mai Restaurant, Krabi — an award-winning Thai restaurant set in a traditional wooden house, renowned for its authentic Krabi-style crab curry and slow-cooked pork dishes

day_by_day.notes: Phra Nang Cave Beach houses a sacred fertility shrine — be respectful of the offerings. The sandbar at Tup Island is tide-dependent; your guide will time the visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Railay Beach by longtail boat from Krabi (15-minute journey) — this car-free peninsula is only accessible by water and is home to some of Thailand's most dramatic scenery. Explore East and West Railay beaches in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing session on Railay's world-famous limestone karsts with a certified instructor — routes cater to all levels, and the views from the top are extraordinary. Alternatively, explore the hidden Railay Lagoon via a short jungle hike.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at the Last Bar on Railay Beach — a legendary beach bar with fire shows and a laid-back atmosphere. Watch the fire dancers perform as the stars emerge over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast — yoghurt, granola, fresh fruit, and Thai-style omelette
meals.lunch: Railay Beach Club — fresh coconut, grilled fish tacos, and cold beers with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Grotto Bar & Restaurant, Railay — built into a natural limestone cave, offering seafood and Thai dishes in one of Thailand's most atmospheric dining settings

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats to Railay depart from Krabi's Chao Fah Pier regularly. Rock climbing should be booked with a reputable operator — Railay Rock Climbing School is highly regarded. The lagoon hike involves some rope-assisted scrambling; wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Krabi to Ao Nang (20 minutes). Spend the morning exploring Ao Nang's beach promenade and local markets. Visit a local Thai massage school for a premium 90-minute traditional Thai massage to rejuvenate after a week of activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private longtail boat to explore the quieter beaches north of Ao Nang — Noppharat Thara Beach and the outer islands of Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park. Snorkel in pristine waters away from the crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang for dinner. Explore the bustling Ao Nang Walking Street for street food — grilled corn, fresh spring rolls, satay, and Thai desserts. End the evening with cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the bay.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang street food breakfast — roti with egg and curry, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and Thai-style pancakes
meals.lunch: Beachside seafood lunch on Noppharat Thara — fresh grilled prawns, steamed clams, and som tam (green papaya salad)
meals.dinner: Azzurra Ao Nang Restaurant — Italian-Thai fusion fine dining with fresh imported ingredients, wood-fired pizza, and an impressive wine list overlooking the Andaman

day_by_day.notes: Ao Nang is a convenient base with excellent transport links. If returning to Krabi for the night, arrange a private driver. October evenings can bring brief rain showers — carry a compact umbrella.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure by private speedboat or ferry to Koh Lanta (approximately 2 hours from Krabi). Check in to a luxury beachfront resort on Koh Lanta Yai. Spend the morning relaxing on the long, uncrowded beach in front of the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) — a charming stilted fishing village with Sino-Portuguese architecture, independent boutiques, and artisan cafés. Visit a local spice shop and pick up authentic Thai condiments to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's private beach. Watch the sky turn dramatic shades of orange and purple over the Andaman Sea — Koh Lanta is renowned for its spectacular west-facing sunsets.

meals.breakfast: Final Krabi hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Old Town café lunch in Koh Lanta — fresh fish cakes, coconut soup, and cold pressed juices at a heritage shophouse café
meals.dinner: Mango House Restaurant, Koh Lanta Old Town — a converted heritage house serving refined Thai cuisine with fresh local seafood and an extensive cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta has a more relaxed, upscale atmosphere compared to busier islands — ideal for a mid-trip wind-down. The old town is best explored on foot or by rented bicycle.

day_by_day.morning: Join a private snorkelling and diving day trip to the Koh Lanta Marine National Park — covering the stunning islands of Koh Rok Nok, Koh Rok Nai, and Koh Ha. These southern islands boast some of the clearest water and most pristine coral in the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkelling at Koh Ha's underwater caves and swim-throughs. Enjoy a gourmet seafood lunch on board the private charter. Afternoon free swim and sunbathing on a deserted white sand beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Indulge in a 2-hour couples' spa package at the resort — traditional Thai massage, herbal steam, and aromatherapy body wrap.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs your way, tropical fruits, fresh-baked pastries, and barista coffee on the beachfront terrace
meals.lunch: On-board gourmet lunch during the marine park tour — grilled fish, rice dishes, fresh fruits, and soft drinks
meals.dinner: Time for a Lime Cooking School & Restaurant, Koh Lanta — a celebrated local institution offering an evening dining experience with dishes from their famous cooking school kitchen

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok and Koh Ha are within the national park — entry fees apply. Visibility is typically excellent in October as the monsoon clears. Book the marine park trip through your resort concierge for the best private operators.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a private scooter or arrange a driver to explore Koh Lanta's interior. Visit the Lanta Animal Welfare Centre — a remarkable NGO caring for street animals — then continue to the southern tip of the island at Mu Ko Lanta National Park for jungle walks and stunning sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely afternoon. Take a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) lesson or rent kayaks to explore the coastline at your own pace. Enjoy a poolside afternoon with tropical cocktails.
day_by_day.evening: Join a private sunset fishing trip with a local fisherman — cast lines for snapper and barracuda as the sun sets, then have your catch prepared by the resort chef for a bespoke private dinner on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast — smoothie bowls, chia pudding, and fresh coconut
meals.lunch: Beachside BBQ at the resort — marinated chicken skewers, grilled vegetables, and papaya salad
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner — your fresh catch of the day prepared by the resort's head chef, served under the stars with Thai sides, jasmine rice, and a curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner should be arranged with the resort at least 24 hours in advance. The national park entrance at the southern tip charges a small fee. Wear insect repellent for the jungle walk.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Lanta — take a slow sunrise walk along the beach, collect shells, and enjoy a peaceful breakfast. Visit a local market near Ban Saladan pier for last-minute souvenir shopping — handmade batik fabrics, local honey, and dried spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer back to Krabi (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check in to a luxury hotel near Krabi Airport or Ao Nang for the final night. Spend the afternoon at the hotel's infinity pool with views over the karst landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Final celebratory dinner in Krabi — a premium seafood feast to mark the end of an extraordinary journey through Thailand's southern islands.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast spread — a final indulgent morning meal with all the tropical favourites
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a Krabi café upon arrival — fresh baguettes, Thai iced tea, and fruit shakes
meals.dinner: Sala Krabi Restaurant — an upscale riverside restaurant with panoramic views, specialising in whole grilled lobster, southern Thai curries, and an exceptional dessert menu

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the speedboat transfer timing with your operator the night before. Krabi Airport is approximately 15 minutes from most Ao Nang hotels — arrange a private transfer for departure day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel. Take a short stroll through Krabi Town one final time, stop at a local café for a farewell Thai iced coffee, and browse any remaining shops for gifts and keepsakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Krabi International Airport (KBV) for departure. Arrive at least 2 hours before your international flight. Relax in the airport lounge if available.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Krabi — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days across Thailand's most beautiful beaches, islands, and culinary landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, pastries, and premium Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or pre-departure meal at a Krabi Town restaurant — a final bowl of khao man gai (poached chicken rice) or boat noodles as a farewell to Thai cuisine
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Krabi Airport has limited luxury lounge facilities — if your airline offers lounge access, confirm availability in advance. Reconfirm your return flight 24 hours before departure. Ensure all souvenirs comply with customs regulations — particularly fresh fruits, spices, and any wildlife products.
